text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- The ruling Labour Party, which faces elections next month, receives more than 10 million crowns in donations from the trade unions this year while the Conservatives get six million from the Confederation of Industry and private donors.
- The number of foreigners working in the construction and offshore industry has increased by almost 25 percent since last year.
- The use of ecstasy mainly among young people has grown strongly in the past three years and the price of the illegal drug has been cut in half.
- Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's largest bank, recorded net profits of 1,494 million crowns in the first half of 1997, compared with 1,489 million in the corresponding period last year.

- Telecommunications company Nera ASA booked first half pre-tax profits at 66.4 million crowns, up 18 percent, or 10 million crowns from a year ago. Nera, Norway's largest manufacturer of wireless telecommunications equipment and systems, said that after a relatively weak first quarter, orders and sales improved during the second three-month period.
- A recent report from Christiania Markets says Ocean Rig ASA is excessively priced and the broker house recommends it's clients to sell their shares in Ocean Rig.
